description: Tests 4 and 5 load a real fixture (anchor_permitted_dns.der, generated by pyca/cryptography), decode it to Certificate, then replace the NC extension's extn_value with b"\xff\xff" (invalid DER). This tests the exact parse path used in production (OctetString::as_bytes() fed to NameConstraints::from_der). The alternative — generating a fixture file whose extension already contains invalid DER — would be harder to audit (the generator would have to deliberately produce malformed output), and harder to trace back to a known-good oracle. The mutation approach separates concerns: the fixture proves the cert structure is correct (pyca/cryptography is the oracle for that), while the in-memory corruption precisely targets the one failure mode under test. A future contributor might suggest replacing mutation with a synthetic cert built entirely in test code. That would test an untested code path (construction from raw fields) rather than the actual production deserialization path, and would lose the oracle provenance.
title: Malformed-NC test uses in-memory mutation of valid fixture DER, not a hand-crafted synthetic cert
